messages:
izzy: Hey @ben @dina — ACME (customer: acme-corp) just opened a ticket: p99 generation latency jumped ~3.5x 10m ago and lots of 429s + some 504s. They reported increased failures when they hit our API concurrently from a batch job.
ben: on it. can you paste the customer request example and the org id?
izzy: Org ID: org_8321. sample header: `POST /v1/generate` payload ~1200 tokens, streaming disabled. They say traffic is mostly bursty with spikes of ~200 rps for ~30s bursts.
dina: seeing matching spike on ingress metrics for org_8321 around 2141599800. Admission queue depth spiked to ~480 for the inferencer pool handling that tenant. p95 latency for that pool jumped from 280ms -> 1.1s, p99 from 820ms -> 2.9s.
raj: any auth or billing errors? Admission rejects sometimes when tokens/concurrency reached?
izzy: Customer saw a few `insufficient_quota` 402s (billing fallback) but most are 429/timeout. They said they retried and saw more 429s.
ci-bot: [deploy] rollout/ingress-admission-patch started by @dina at 2141600200 :eyes:
dina: quick checks: the affected pool is using model variant `gpt-neo-8b-q4` on 4xA100 shared nodes. Per-node concurrency limit is 32; autoscaler didn't spin up because burst < 1min. The admission controller queue length limit is 400, then we go to rejecting mode. We hit the soft limit ~2141599820 and then hard limit ~2141599855.
ben: that fits. bursts cause queue buildup and admission triggers hard rejects. we should avoid full queue if downstream is slow. proposed quick mitigations: 1) enable tenant-specific fast-fail (drop requests over concurrency threshold) 2) route spike to a smaller/faster model variant (gpt-neo-2.7b-fp16) 3) temporarily raise admission soft limit for this pool while we autoscale.
izzy: ACME is asking for root cause and repro steps. They can reproduce with their batch job (200 rps bursts). I can request a replay token.
raj: for customer-facing patch, prefer options 1+2 (fast-fail + fallback) — less risk than changing global admission limits. Can we hotpatch admission rules for org_8321?
dina: yes. admin command available: 
```
redwoodctl admission update --org org_8321 --policy fast-fail=true --fallback-model gpt-neo-2.7b-fp16 --fast-fail-threshold 28
```
I'll run that as a canary for 10m targeting only that tenant.
ben: also add temporary logging to capture request ids that hit fallback so we can correlate to customer traces: `admission.log.fallback_ids=true` for org_8321.
izzy: sent the short repro instructions + temporary mitigation plan to ACME support thread. They asked for a deeper postmortem: why autoscaler didn't scale.
dina: autoscaler eval shows average GPU utilization per node 78% during the burst; scaling policy requires sustained >85% for 45s to add a node. since bursts were ~30s autoscaler never acted. That's intended to avoid flapping.
raj: note to product: we might want a burst policy that allows ephemeral burst capacity (burst seconds) for customers above X rps. filing ticket after this.
ben: immediate hotpatch completed: applied fast-fail + fallback at 2141600305. initial telemetry shows queue depth dropped from 470 -> 60 within 30s and p99 back down to ~900ms. ACME reports fewer 429s. :thumbsup:
acme-cust-john: Thanks — we saw errors drop, but a subset of jobs now got shorter outputs because they hit fallback model. Is there any way to keep quality?
ben: for now fallback reduces latency at cost of output length/quality. we can add a model-chaining fallback: try fast model with `max_tokens=800` then requeue full model for async completion. longer term, recommend dedicated capacity for predictable SLAs.
izzy: next steps checklist: 
- [x] apply tenant fast-fail + fallback (dina)
- [x] enable fallback logging (ben)
- [x] collect traces & traces exported to support S3 for postmortem (dina)
- [ ] prod ticket for autoscaler burst policy (raj)
- [ ] follow-up with ACME about dedicated capacity offer (sales)

ben: for ops runbook update: add a section for "bursty tenant mitigation" with commands and monitoring playbook. I'll add a short PR.
dina: adding metrics we watched: `ingress.qdepth.org_8321`, `node.gpu.util`, `admission.rejected.org_8321`, `fallback.count.org_8321`. dashboards: https://dash.redwood.local/d/ingress/tenant-overview
izzy: closing the support escalation for now — reopened if ACME sees fresh spikes. thanks all. :heart:
